title: Stochastic Voronoi Ensembles for Anomaly Detection
summary: Anomaly detection is challenging when data exhibits varying local densities, as distance-based methods miss local anomalies and density-based approaches incur quadratic computational costs. This paper proposes SVEAD, which constructs an ensemble of random Voronoi diagrams and scores points by normalized cell-relative distances weighted by local scale. Experiments on 45 benchmark datasets demonstrate that SVEAD achieves state-of-the-art AUC-ROC and AUC-PR while maintaining linear time complexity and constant space complexity.

match_target.why: This is the cheapest claim to reproduce (single small dataset, CPU-only, seconds) while directly demonstrating SVEAD's core anomaly detection performance on a real-world healthcare benchmark.

tolerance.why: Rule 1 applies: the paper reports a standard deviation of 0.0063 over 5 runs for this value; 3 × 0.0063 = 0.0189, rounded up to the 4-decimal precision used in the paper gives 0.019.

requirements.stmt: Sample anchor sets uniformly from the dataset without replacement for each partition
Assign each point to its nearest anchor to form Voronoi cells
Compute within-cell anomaly score as the product of relative position normalization and mean distance
Aggregate scores across partitions by arithmetic mean

requirements.quote: The total time complexity is O(nmdt) + O(nmdt) = O(nmdt)

requirements.stmt: Use grid search over anchor count m ∈ {21, 22, ..., 28} with fixed ensemble size t=100
requirements.quote: the number of sample points is searched over {21, 22, . . . , 28}, with ensemble size fixed at 100

requirements.stmt: Repeat experiments 5 times and report average performance
requirements.quote: For each dataset and method, we repeat experiments 5 times and report the average performance

requirements.stmt: Operate in the unsupervised anomaly detection setting
requirements.quote: We focus on the unsupervised anomaly detection setting where X contains an unknown mixture of normal instances and anomalous instances

requirements.stmt: Evaluate using AUC-ROC and AUC-PR metrics
requirements.quote: We adopt Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic curve (AUC-ROC) and Area Under the Precision-Recall curve (AUC-PR) in the experiment

requirements.stmt: Skip scoring for points in cells containing only the anchor
requirements.quote: In the rare case where a cell contains only the anchor (|Ci| = 1), we skip scoring for this point in this partition and rely on the other t − 1 partitions in the ensemble average
